EllipticCurveModularity.summary: Nothing of the modularity argument itself is in the libraries. Both trees have substantial elliptic-curve and modular-form infrastructure that the roadmap correctly treats as existing input: Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve/IsElliptic, minimal models and reduction types (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Reduction.lean), and — a target the roadmap document does not credit — Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.LFunction / WeierstrassCurve.LSeries over an arbitrary number field, with the local Euler factors 1 - a_p T + q T^2, 1 - T, 1 + T, 1 already defined at every prime including the bad ones. Tau Ceti adds isogenies, the Hom group with degree and the additive pullback of the invariant differential, point counts and WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace, plus a full bundled newform theory (HeckeRing.GL2.Newform, multiplicity one, strong multiplicity one, Sturm-bound finite-dimensionality of cusp forms and the entire continuation of a cusp form's coefficient L-series). What is genuinely missing is everything in between: there is no Galois representation attached to an elliptic curve (no Weil pairing, no E[p] as a Galois module, no Tate module), no conductor of an elliptic curve, no Faltings finiteness/isogeny theorem, no Serre modularity, no modular curve X_0(N), no Jacobian J_0(N) and no abelian variety A_f. The Abel-Jacobi map is a partial exception the roadmap document does not credit: Tau Ceti builds the base-point-normalised Abel-Jacobi divisor-class map D |-> [D - deg(D).x_0] into an abstract Pic^0, with the symmetric-power Abel map and the theorem that its fibres are complete linear systems, all before any Jacobian variety exists. Every layer R29.1-R29.6 is not built.

targets.target: End_Q(E) = Z for an elliptic curve over Q
targets.note: Tau Ceti builds Hom(W1,W2) as an abelian group with degree, composition and negation (Isogeny/Hom/{Basic,Add,Neg}.lean) and an endomorphism ring of an abelian variety, but proves nothing about its rank; the only computation of an End ring is AbelianVariety.End.instUnique for the trivial variety. No statement End_Q(E) = Z or End = Z-span of [n] exists in either library.

targets.target: Injectivity in characteristic zero of the derivative on the invariant differential, on the endomorphism algebra
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the map f |-> f^*omega and proves it additive (Silverman III.5.2), that [n]^*omega = n.omega, and the differential criterion isSeparable iff f^*omega != 0. The characteristic-zero injectivity statement that R29.1 wants (f^*omega = 0 implies f = 0, hence End embeds in the base field) is not drawn; the criterion is used only for 1 - Frobenius over a finite field.

targets.target: Faltings: finitely many Q-isomorphism classes in a Q-isogeny class
targets.note: No occurrence of Faltings, of a height bound on isogenous curves, or of finiteness of an isogeny class in either tree (grep -rn -i faltings returns nothing in TauCeti/ and mathlib/).

targets.target: Hom_Q(E,E') free of rank one when End_Q(E) = Z, so map degrees are d.n^2; only finitely many prime degrees occur
targets.note: deg(n.f) is computed, which is the n^2 factor of the wanted degree formula, but Hom is never shown free of rank one and no finiteness of the set of rational prime isogeny degrees is stated.

targets.target: Reducible E[p] gives a rational cyclic p-isogeny; E[p] is F_p-irreducible for all but finitely many p; absolute irreducibility for odd p from oddness
targets.note: E[p] is never made into a Galois module: there is no Galois action on torsion points anywhere in either library (the only Galois material under EllipticCurve/ is descent of Weierstrass data and quadratic twists), and the Weil pairing itself is not constructed — Tau Ceti has built the first inputs of its divisor construction (Silverman III.8), namely that n(T) - n(O) is principal at an n-torsion point, divisor evaluation and disjoint-support machinery, but the pairing is repeatedly named there as work not yet done. Irreducibility, reducibility and the induced cyclic isogeny are therefore all absent.

duplicates.note: Explicitly states the same targets: 'Prove the finite-generation and rank-one Hom consequence when End_Q(E)=Z. R29 uses this to show only finitely many rational prime-degree isogenies' — the Hom rank-one and finite-prime-degree conclusions of R29.1 are its exports.
Owns 'finiteness of the relevant isomorphism classes within an isogeny class', the Faltings input R29.1 restates.
Owns the Tate isogeny theorem and Hom_F(A,B) tensor Q_l = Hom_{G_F}(V_l A, V_l B), the rational Hom comparison R29.1 uses to bound Hom ranks.

targets.target: Apply the strong Serre modularity theorem to E[p] for infinitely many good p >= 5
targets.note: Serre's modularity conjecture in any form is absent: no declaration or docstring mentioning a residual modularity statement exists in either tree, and the residual representation E[p] itself is not constructed.

targets.target: Finite flatness at p gives Serre weight two and prime-to-p conductor dividing N_E
targets.note: No Serre weight and no Serre conductor N(rho-bar) exists, and 'p-divisible' has zero hits in both trees. The nearest groundwork is Tau Ceti's Cartier duality for commutative finite locally free group schemes in Hopf-algebra form, which is a prerequisite for finite flat group schemes rather than the theory itself.

targets.target: Weight-two level-dividing-N newform attached to the residual representation, with trivial nebentypus from determinant compatibility, after excluding primes dividing phi(N_E)
targets.note: The carrier exists — Tau Ceti's bundled Newform N k of level Gamma_1(N), weight k and nebentypus chi, with the new subspace and the a_1 = 1 normalisation — and TrivialNebentypus.lean handles the trivial-character case. What is missing is any link from a Galois representation to such a form: the whole content of the layer.

targets.target: Record coefficient fields and primes above p of the resulting newforms
targets.note: Tau Ceti's newforms are complex-analytic (coefficients in C); there is no coefficient number field K_f, no ring of integers of K_f and no choice of a prime above p attached to a newform.

duplicates.note: Owns the theorem being applied and says so: 'Export the finite-flat weight-two bounded-level consequence used by R29'.
Owns local residual types and Serre weights, i.e. the finite-flatness-implies-weight-two step R29.2 restates.
Owns the level-changing algebra that produces the bound on the prime-to-p conductor.

targets.target: Only finitely many normalised newforms of weight two and level dividing N, including coefficient embeddings
targets.note: The two ingredients are proved sorry-free — finite-dimensionality of CuspForm for any finite-relative-index subgroup of GL(2,R) (Sturm bound), and that each new Hecke eigenspace is one-dimensional — but the conclusion 'the set of newforms of level N and weight k is finite' is nowhere assembled; there is no Finite (Newform N k) instance.

targets.target: a_l(f) - a_l(E) an algebraic integer divisible by primes over infinitely many p, so its integer norm vanishes and a_l(f) = a_l(E) for every good l
targets.note: Both sides of the comparison exist separately: a_q(E) = q + 1 - #W(F_q) as WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace, and a_n(f) as the newform's Hecke eigenvalue. No congruence, divisibility or equality between them is stated, and there is no algebraic-integer norm argument of this shape in either library. Tau Ceti's TauCeti/Data/Int/CongrAllPrimes.lean has the elementary 'an integer divisible by all but finitely many primes is zero' pattern, but only for rational integers.

targets.target: Rationality of the coefficient field via Galois conjugation and strong multiplicity one, including the bad coefficients
targets.note: Strong multiplicity one is fully proved in Tau Ceti (Miyake Thm 4.6.12), in exactly the strong form R29.3 needs: agreement of eigenvalues outside a finite set of good indices forces equality, so nothing at all is assumed at indices dividing the level. Missing are the Galois conjugate f^sigma of a newform, the coefficient field K_f, and hence the rationality argument itself.

targets.target: Comparison of V_r(E) with the r-adic representation of f by Chebotarev, characteristic polynomials and semisimplicity
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a Chebotarev development in progress (FrobeniusPrimeSet, ramified primes, Galois-character weights, von Mangoldt prime counting) but no Tate module of an elliptic curve and no Galois representation attached to a modular form, so the comparison has neither side.

targets.target: Full local-global compatibility with monodromy identifying conductors at the bad primes
targets.note: No Weil-Deligne representations, no monodromy operator N, no local-global compatibility statement exists in either library.

targets.target: The primitive level of f equals N_E exactly
targets.note: The conductor of an elliptic curve is not defined anywhere: Mathlib's Reduction.lean classifies reduction types over a DVR but defines no exponent f_p or global conductor, and there is no Tate algorithm, Kodaira type or Neron model in either tree.

targets.target: Equality of bad local Euler factors, and Tate-module comparisons at all auxiliary primes
targets.note: One side is built and the roadmap does not say so: Mathlib defines the local Euler factor of a Weierstrass curve at every prime of a number field, with the four cases 1 - a_p T + q T^2 (good), 1 - T (split multiplicative), 1 + T (nonsplit multiplicative), 1 (additive), all sorry-free. The newform's local factors at bad primes, and any equality between the two, are absent.

duplicates.note: Owns the Galois representation attached to a weight-two newform and the unramified characteristic polynomial via Eichler-Shimura; R29.4 compares that object with V_r(E).
Restates the bad-prime Euler-factor comparison, 'prove every local Euler-factor comparison, including bad primes', for the twisted L-function; it lists R29.4-R29.6 as its dependency.

targets.target: A_f as a quotient of J_0(N_E) for a weight-two trivial-nebentypus newform, with K_f = Q and dim A_f = 1
targets.note: Neither J_0(N) nor any Jacobian of a curve exists in the libraries; Tau Ceti's AlgebraicGeometry/Curves/StableReduction/Picard is a Picard group of a stable curve over a DVR, not a Jacobian variety over Q, and the AbelianVariety files give only the general Hom/End/isogeny notions.

targets.target: Isogeny A_f -> E over Q from the Tate-module identification and the isogeny theorem
targets.note: The notion of isogeny of abelian varieties exists; the Tate isogeny theorem that would produce this particular one does not (see R29.1).

targets.target: The composite X_0(N_E) -> J_0(N_E) -> A_f -> E of the cusp-normalised Abel-Jacobi map, and its nonconstancy
targets.note: The base-point-normalised Abel-Jacobi map exists in Tau Ceti at divisor-class level and the roadmap does not credit it: for an abstract order system with a weight-one base point x_0 it builds x |-> [x - w(x).x_0] and D |-> [D - deg(D).x_0] into an abstract Pic^0, the symmetric-power Abel map D |-> O(D - d.x_0), and proves that two effective divisors of the same degree have equal class exactly when they are linearly equivalent, so the fibres are complete linear systems - all sorry-free. Its own docstrings say it is available 'before line bundles, the Picard scheme, or the Jacobian variety exist'. Missing are the modular curve X_0(N) as a scheme ('modular curve' has zero hits in both trees), J_0(N), the morphism to an abelian variety, the rational cusp as base point, and any nonconstancy or 'the curve generates its Jacobian' statement. Tau Ceti's Cusps files are cusps of a congruence subgroup acting on the upper half plane, not rational points of an algebraic modular curve.

duplicates.note: Owns exactly the quotient construction R29.5 applies: 'construct its Hecke ideal and the quotient A_f of J_1(N), or J_0(N) for trivial character, as an abelian variety over Q ... Prove the quotient map and Abel-Jacobi composite are nonzero where required'.
Supplies 'the rational cusp and normalised Abel-Jacobi map used by R29', the normalisation R29.5 composes with.
Also constructs a pushforward along a modular parametrisation to E, but states the parametrisation as a hypothesis to be discharged from the modularity family rather than proving it.
Maps CM points through 'the existing modular quotient' to E and lists EllipticCurveModularity R29.5 as a dependency; consumer overlap rather than a second construction.

targets.target: The unconditional modularity theorem: for every elliptic curve over Q a weight-two rational newform of exact conductor N_E and a nonconstant Q-morphism X_0(N_E) -> E
targets.note: Absent, as are all of its ingredients (R29.1-R29.5). No declaration or docstring in either tree asserts modularity of elliptic curves; every grep hit for 'modularity' is modular-lattice or submodularity vocabulary.

targets.target: Equivalence with the Frobenius-coefficient formulation a_p(E) = a_p(f)
targets.note: Both sides of the identity a_q = q + 1 - #E(F_q) = a_q(f) are defined sorry-free in Tau Ceti — frobeniusTrace is stated for every Weierstrass model, deliberately counting the singular point so that it returns 1, -1, 0 at split multiplicative, nonsplit multiplicative and additive reduction — but nothing relates them.

targets.target: Analytic continuation and functional equation of L(E,s), transferred after proving equality of every local factor
targets.note: Both endpoints of the transfer exist. Mathlib defines the elliptic curve's L-function as an Euler product over the height-one spectrum of the ring of integers and its LSeries as a complex function; Mathlib's ModularForm.Λ/CuspForm.differentiable_L and Tau Ceti's CuspForm.hasEntireExtension_qExpansion_coeff give the entire continuation on the modular side, and Tau Ceti's ModularForm.LSeries_qExpansion_coeff_eq identifies the coefficient Dirichlet series with Mathlib's L. The transfer needs equality of the two Dirichlet series, which needs modularity.

duplicates.note: States that its alternative route 'deduce[s] the same R29 elliptic-curve theorem through a theorem parameter or a separate corollary' — the same endpoint reached by a second argument.
Builds 'the interface from the Euler product/Dirichlet series of E to its modular entire continuation and completed functional equation', which is the analytic half of R29.6.

EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceCompari.summary: Nothing in this roadmap exists in either library, and the gap is not marginal: a case-insensitive grep of both trees returns zero hits for endoscop, transfer factor, orbital integral, Tate-Nakayama, Kottwitz, Shalika, pseudocoefficient, Satake, Jacquet, Jacquet-Langlands, Lubin-Tate, perverse, nearby cycle, Hitchin and affine Springer; the phrase 'fundamental lemma' occurs only in the calculus of variations, the Selberg sieve and homotopical algebra. There is no smooth representation theory of p-adic groups at all; Tau Ceti's representation theory of GL_2 is over a finite field (character tables, principal series, cuspidal representations of GL_2(F_q)), and its p-adic side stops at local fields and central simple algebras. The ambient scaffolding the roadmap would build on does exist in places: Tau Ceti has affine algebraic groups in Hopf-algebra form with reductivity, Borel and parabolic/Levi (dynamic-method) theory, isogenies and split tori, plus continuous cohomology of profinite groups; Mathlib has adele rings, Haar measure, abstract t-structures with hearts, and l-adic cohomology as pro-etale sheaf cohomology of Z_l. None of that touches the roadmap's targets. Three of the fifteen layers (ET.2a and its two prefixes) are re-export layers that construct nothing of their own and are marked process; the other twelve are not built.

targets.note: No occurrence of 'stable conjugacy', 'stably conjugate' or 'inner twist' in either tree. Tau Ceti's only semisimple-conjugacy computations are conjugacy class sizes in GL_2(F_q) (LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Centralizer.lean).

GL2ModularityLifting.summary: No modularity-lifting theorem, and none of its ingredients, exists in either library. There are no Galois deformation rings (zero hits for deformation functor, Schlessinger, prorepresentable, pseudorepresentation), no Galois representations attached to modular forms, no Barsotti-Tate or finite flat group schemes, no de Rham or crystalline conditions, and no Taylor-Wiles patching. What does exist is the Hecke side's raw material: Mathlib's abstract Hecke ring of a Hecke pair with arbitrary coefficients, Tau Ceti's GL_2 instantiation at Gamma_0(N)/Gamma_1(N) with multiplication tables and the action on cusp forms, and the bundled newform theory with multiplicity one and strong multiplicity one; and on the commutative-algebra side Mathlib's regular sequences and the Rees theorem for depth. Even these fall short of the layers' targets: the Hecke algebras are complex-analytic Hecke operators on C-vector spaces of cusp forms, not integral Hecke algebras localised at a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal, and Mathlib has no Cohen-Macaulay theory.
